answer: The page gets the icon from the first tag in its `tags` list that sets one (when several tags set the same field, the first tag wins). If the page sets its own `pageDecoration` (in its frontmatter or via a `transform`), that wins over the tags' decorations.

--- API/tag.md ---
API | API > tag.define(spec)
Defines a tag explicitly.

`spec` is a table that can contain:
* `name` (required) the name of the tag
* `tagPage` page to navigate to when clicking the tag (defaults to `tag:name`)
* `metatable` to set a custom Lua metatable for objects with this tag.
* `mustValidate` a boolean defining whether or not schema validation must pass for the object to be indexed
* `schema` [[Schema]] to validate against
* `icon` a [Feather](https://feathericons.com) icon name for the tag itself, shown in the [[Workbench]]. Unlike `pageDecoration`, it doesn't decorate the tag's pages; when it's absent, `pageDecoration.icon` is used.
* `pageDecoration` [[Page Decorations|page decoration]] (`icon`, `prefix`, `cssClasses`, …) for every page with this tag. See [[Page Decorations#Apply to every page with a tag]].
* `validate` callback function invoked when an objects needs to be validated, returns `nil` or an error message.

--- Tag/page.md ---
page
Every page in your space is available via the `page` tag. You can attach _additional_ tags to a page, by either specifying them in the `tags` attribute [[Frontmatter]], or by putting additional [[Tag|tags]] in a standalone paragraph with no other (textual) content in them.

The field reference below describes the stable attributes. This query shows their values and any additional frontmatter on the current page:

${query[[from index.pages() where name == _CTX.currentPage.name]]}

--- Tag/tag.md ---
tag
The `tag` tag indexes the tags themselves: for each page, one record per tag used on it and the root tag of the objects it is used on. This is what powers `#` completion and the [[Tag Picker]].

--- Workbench/Data.md ---
The tag list | The tag list
Tags from [[Tag/data|data blocks]] carry a small `data` label. Drag the list's right edge to make it wider; double-click the edge to reset it. Typing in the filter narrows every section; Enter picks the first match. Each tag shows its icon: a tag's `icon`, or else the icon of its `pageDecoration` (see [[API/tag]]).

--- Page Decorations.md ---
Supported decorations | Apply to every page with a tag
To decorate every page with a tag, give the tag a `pageDecoration` in [[API/tag|tag.define]] in your [[CONFIG]]:

```lua
tag.define {
  name = "person",
  pageDecoration = { icon = "user", cssClasses = { "person-page" } },
}
```

A page’s own `pageDecoration` (from its frontmatter, or a `transform`) wins over the tag’s. When several of a page’s tags set the same field, the first tag in its `tags` wins. `cssClasses` from all of them are combined. Changing a tag’s decoration re-indexes the pages with that tag, so there is no need to run `Space: Reindex`.
